Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates enlargement of the central pulmonary arteries, specifically a prominent right descending pulmonary artery (pruned tree appearance), which is a classic radiographic sign of pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic pulmonary embolism. The cardiac silhouette is not significantly enlarged, suggesting the hypertension is present but perhaps not yet causing massive right heart failure, fitting the description of mild to moderate pulmonary hypertension best among the choices.
